**Resolved — no incident. The maintainer merged it.**

Provenance, all three parts: **who** — the maintainer; **verbatim** — 「5188 是我合并的」; **where** — said directly to the `repo:objectui` PM seat in session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`, 2026-08-18, in response to this card's determination request.

That is the answer this card existed to get. objectui PR #5188 / `4eac264` is a **recognised** governed merge. No violation, no rollback, and the seat discipline held — PR5124, PR5080 and PR4930 remain untouched and awaiting a human merge. Closing `not planned`.

## One inference in this card was wrong, and I am correcting it rather than leaving it on the record

I wrote, under prism 3, that the prohibition in the PR body "was stated in the strongest available place… and it still did not bind", concluding that prose in a PR body is not a control surface. **That conclusion was premised on a violation that did not happen.** The prohibition addressed AI seats; the human it did not address is the one who merged. It was never tested, so it cannot be said to have failed. Struck.

## What genuinely survives, and it is sharper than what I filed

`merged_by` on this merge reads **`os-steve`** — a seat account — and the merge was performed by the maintainer. So:

> **`merged_by` cannot distinguish a maintainer merge from an AI-seat merge, because the maintainer also operates the seat accounts.**

This is the shared-identity trap from the claim protocol showing up in a second place. In the claim protocol the documented workaround is the session ID in the claim comment; **a merge carries no such discriminator at all.**

The consequence lands squarely on #9619's attribution half, and it makes that card *more* important rather than less: I filed it asking for `merged_by` to be resolved, on the assumption that resolving it would answer "does the maintainer recognise this entry". **It would not have.** Resolving the column here would have returned `os-steve` and left the question exactly as open as it was — which is why this took a direct question to the maintainer to settle. A fix for #9619 that merely supplies a token is therefore insufficient by construction. I have recorded this on #9619.

The practical reading for any seat that finds itself here again: a governed merge attributed to a seat account is **not** evidence of a violation. It is evidence of an unanswered question, and the only instrument that answers it is asking the maintainer. Filing the card and asking — rather than reverting on the inference — was the right shape, and remains the right shape next time.
